source_text: ἐναντίων αἰσχύνην ἄντικρυς ἀραμένων. 34 Οἱ δὲ φθόνῳ τὸ μῖσος ἀράμενοι κατ' αὐτοῦ καὶ πεφραγμένοι πολεμίᾳ παρατάξει σκορπίζονται, τοῦ Λόγου τε καὶ Θεοῦ τὸν ἑαυτοῦ ναὸν ἀξιοπρεπῶς ἀναστήσαντος.
thought_title: Shame of enemies and scattering by the Word's raising of his temple
orientation: Eustathius is closing his argument that acquired glory belongs to the man of Christ, not to the Father or the Word, and now describes the fate of Christ's enemies.
pass_a_gloss: his enemies having openly taken up shame. But those who took up hatred against him out of envy and were fenced in by a hostile battle-line are scattered, the Word and God having fittingly raised up his own temple.

choices.english: his enemies having openly taken up shame
choices.why: Keeps the genitive absolute as a dependent clause and renders ἄντικρυς as 'openly' to convey the public, unambiguous nature of the shame.
rejected: the enemies having taken up shame outright
his enemies having taken shame openly

choices.term: Οἱ δὲ φθόνῳ τὸ μῖσος ἀράμενοι κατ' αὐτοῦ
choices.english: But those who took up hatred against him out of envy
choices.why: Preserves the participial phrase as the subject and keeps the dative φθόνῳ as 'out of envy' to show motive.
rejected: But those who out of envy took up hatred against him
But the ones having taken up hatred against him by envy

choices.english: were fenced in by a hostile battle-line
choices.why: Renders the perfect passive participle as a finite passive to match the main clause, and keeps the military metaphor of a battle-line as the barrier.
rejected: having been fenced in by a hostile array

choices.why: Uses the present passive to show the ongoing or resultant state of dispersion, matching the Greek tense.

choices.term: τοῦ Λόγου τε καὶ Θεοῦ τὸν ἑαυτοῦ ναὸν ἀξιοπρεπῶς ἀναστήσαντος
choices.english: the Word and God having fittingly raised up his own temple
choices.why: Keeps the genitive absolute as a dependent clause, renders τε καὶ as 'and', and uses 'fittingly' for ἀξιοπρεπῶς to convey the appropriateness of the act.
rejected: the Word and God having raised up his own temple worthily
since the Word and God fittingly raised his own temple

pass_b_english: openly took up shame. But those who, out of envy, took up hatred against him and were fenced in by a hostile battle-line are scattered, since the Word and God fittingly raised his own temple.
